campaigns.ministry: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) / India Semiconductor Mission (ISM)
campaigns.goals: Establish domestic semiconductor fabrication and display manufacturing facilities; promote chip design, equipment manufacturing, and input material supply chains; expand outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) and advanced packaging units; fund targeted research and development programs and build a specialized technical talent pool.
campaigns.funding_information: Funded directly by the Government of India through central budgetary allocations, including an approved outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore for the Semicon 2.0 phase.
campaigns.summary: India's Semiconductor Journey represents a government-directed industrial policy aimed at establishing semiconductor and display fabrication capabilities within the country. The initiative began operationally in 2022 with the introduction of the Semicon India Programme (Semicon 1.0), administered by the India Semiconductor Mission under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. On July 15, 2026, the Union Cabinet approved the secondary phase, designated as Semicon 2.0, with an allocated central outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore. The strategic framework focuses on six specific pillars: integrated circuit design, manufacturing machinery and raw materials, commercial fab construction, assembly and testing (ATMP/OSAT) facilities, domestic research and development, and specialized workforce training. To supplement physical industrial establishment, the government operates an outreach campaign on the MyGov platform. This digital component hosts competitive assessments, technical quizzes, and citizen consultation forums to solicit research ideas on artificial intelligence hardware and semiconductor design, tracking public submissions for downstream policy and academic review. The initiative ultimately seeks to reduce the country's reliance on imported microelectronics by directly financing local manufacturing infrastructure.

campaigns.ministry: Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (All India Radio) / Prime Minister's Office
campaigns.goals: Establish a regular direct communication channel from the Prime Minister to the general public; document and broadcast regional grassroots initiatives, environmental conservation efforts, and individual social projects; collect public suggestions, audio recordings, and topic proposals for upcoming broadcast episodes.
campaigns.funding_information: Funded under the regular broadcasting and operational expenditure budgets of All India Radio / Prasar Bharati and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
campaigns.summary: Mann Ki Baat is a monthly radio address delivered by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, first broadcast on October 3, 2014, across the national network of All India Radio. Coordinated administratively by the Prime Minister's Office and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, the program functions as an institutional platform for addressing domestic policy, civic projects, and regional developments. The broadcast is subsequently transcribed, translated into multiple recognized Indian languages, and disseminated via television networks, online audio repositories, and print publications. The associated MyGov digital portal functions as a records archive and interactive reception desk. It allows citizens to submit commentary, propose discussion themes, and upload audio recordings, which are vetted by administrative teams prior to each recording. The web portal also produces structured e-books, statistical breakdowns of highlighted initiatives, and topical summaries of individual episodes, serving as an ongoing public communication channel financed through Prasar Bharati's standard broadcast operations. It operates to provide a standardized state communication mechanism bridging federal governance and local communities.

campaigns.when_it_was_started: July 24, 2026 (commemorating the introduction of income tax on July 24, 1860)
campaigns.ministry: Ministry of Finance (Central Board of Direct Taxes / Income Tax Department)
campaigns.goals: Promote awareness regarding voluntary tax compliance and direct tax filing responsibilities; disseminate operational information regarding the newly implemented Income Tax Act, 2025; collect citizen feedback on statutory service standards established under the Taxpayer's Charter.
campaigns.funding_information: Funded through the public relations and operational budget allocations of the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.
campaigns.summary: The 167th Income Tax Day campaign was observed on July 24, 2026, commemorating the statutory establishment of direct taxation in India by Sir James Wilson in 1860. Administered by the Central Board of Direct Taxes under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, the annual campaign serves as an operational interface between tax administrators and the public. The 2026 observance integrated the PRARAMBH 2026 educational program, structured specifically to inform individual and corporate taxpayers about the administrative and procedural shifts introduced under the Income Tax Act, 2025. Digital outreach on MyGov included an official Tax Contribution Pledge, a platform collecting specific feedback on the Taxpayer's Charter, and short-form video and poster competitions centered on direct tax literacy. The initiative's overarching operational target is to expand the formal tax base, reduce non-compliance disputes through procedural education, and emphasize revenue generation milestones funded through regular CBDT publicity allocations. The campaign frames direct tax contributions as the primary financial basis for ongoing national infrastructure programs.

campaigns.when_it_was_started: Preparatory campaign phase active in 2026; enumeration scheduled for 2027
campaigns.ministry: Ministry of Home Affairs (Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner of India)
campaigns.goals: Transition national decennial demographic data collection to a fully digital platform using proprietary mobile applications; deploy a self-enumeration digital portal enabling direct online household submissions; conduct structured public information campaigns regarding survey parameters.
campaigns.funding_information: Financed by the Central Government via Union Budget capital and revenue allocations for Census, Surveys, and Statistics under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
campaigns.summary: The Census 2027 campaign represents the official public information rollout for the upcoming decennial population enumeration, conducted by the Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs. Operating under the slogan 'Our Census, Our Development,' the project marks the administrative shift to a fully digitized census process. Primary data collection will occur via dedicated mobile applications operated by official enumerators, paired with an optional self-enumeration web system permitting heads of households to submit their demographic information independently. The MyGov campaign serves as a pre-enumeration public awareness instrument designed to minimize non-response rates and clarify survey timelines before field staff are deployed. Public activities include informational video series, explanatory literature regarding survey parameters, digital quizzes, and media competitions targeting secondary and higher education students. All data aggregation systems, software infrastructure, field operations, and associated public outreach are financed through direct central budgetary grants allocated to the Registrar General to facilitate national governance mapping.

campaigns.when_it_was_started: August 15, 1947 (national origin); specific digital campaign active during July–August 2026
campaigns.goals: Coordinate official digital and ceremonial engagements commemorating India's 80th Independence Day; disseminate factual progress reports regarding domestic defense manufacturing, space exploration, and nuclear power development; facilitate cross-ministerial outreach on welfare schemes.
campaigns.funding_information: Funded through annual central ceremonial and public communication allocations of the Ministry of Defence, supplemented by budgets of participating Union Ministries.
campaigns.summary: The Independence Day Celebrations 2026 campaign represents the digital and civic interface for India's 80th Independence Day commemorations, managed centrally by the Ministry of Defence in coordination with the MyGov platform. In addition to broadcasting the official Red Fort ceremonies and prime ministerial address, the portal aggregates cross-ministerial educational programs. The Ministry of Defence, along with departments handling atomic energy, space, rural development, and tribal welfare, hosted thematic competitions including historical analyses of freedom movements, evaluations of domestic defense manufacturing capabilities, and assessments of civilian nuclear energy frameworks. Specific citizen competitions included the 'Ocean Science for a Viksit Bharat' assessment conducted with the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) and quizzes on national security equipment. The campaign operates as an administrative vehicle to report infrastructure, scientific, and statutory milestones across government departments, funded through standard ministerial information budgets. It centralizes public engagement with defense and science milestones on a single digital repository.

campaigns.ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
campaigns.goals: Promote knowledge of the constitutional principles outlined in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution; facilitate nationwide reading of the Preamble across schools and public institutions; generate verified digital participation certificates.
campaigns.funding_information: Funded through statutory civic education and commemorative budget heads of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
campaigns.summary: The 'Read The Preamble' campaign is an institutional civic education initiative managed by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. It originated on November 19, 2015, when the Government of India officially notified November 26 as Constitution Day ('Samvidhan Divas') to mark the date in 1949 when the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India. The primary operational component of the MyGov campaign is a dedicated digital module that displays the complete, unedited text of the Preamble in English and Hindi. Users navigate the module, complete an online reading verification, and download an official digital certificate bearing the emblem of the Government of India. The portal is integrated into academic calendars, encouraging schools, universities, and public sector undertakings to register mass readings. Administrative expenses, server hosting, and security verifications are funded directly through the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment's designated public education expenditures, serving as a standardized tool for civic education across state and federal institutions.

campaigns.when_it_was_started: May 1, 1956 (agency established); 70th anniversary campaign launched May 1, 2026
campaigns.ministry: Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue / Directorate of Enforcement)
campaigns.goals: Increase public understanding of the statutory framework of PMLA and FEMA; provide verification protocols for citizens to authenticate official agency summonses; publish statistical records of asset seizures and restitution of funds.
campaigns.funding_information: Financed directly under the operational, administrative, and public communication budget of the Directorate of Enforcement, Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.
campaigns.summary: The '70 Years of ED' campaign marks the septuagenary anniversary of the Directorate of Enforcement, which was formed on May 1, 1956, as an enforcement unit under the Department of Economic Affairs and subsequently transferred to the Department of Revenue. The agency functions as India's specialized financial investigations authority, enforcing the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA), the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA), and the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 (FEOA). The MyGov campaign serves as a public transparency measure. Its features include an automated utility allowing individuals to verify the legitimacy of official summonses to prevent fraudulent impersonation, digital access to the Directorate's Annual Report for 2025–26, infographics summarizing restitution totals, and an interactive portal for citizen recommendations on operational practices. Funding is provided entirely through the regular administrative appropriations of the Department of Revenue, positioning the platform as a direct mechanism for disseminating agency metrics and legal mandates to the general public.

campaigns.ministry: Statutory body administratively coordinated through the Ministry of Home Affairs
campaigns.goals: Disseminate information regarding statutory protections of human rights; promote adherence to the Paris Principles; educate citizens on mechanisms for lodging complaints regarding rights violations; distribute official investigations and webcasts.
campaigns.funding_information: Funded through annual central Grants-in-Aid allocated under the Union Budget to statutory autonomous bodies, administered via the Ministry of Home Affairs.
campaigns.summary: The National Human Rights Commission campaign functions as a public education interface for India's independent statutory human rights oversight institution. Established on October 12, 1993, pursuant to the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 (amended in 2019), the Commission operates in conformity with the United Nations Paris Principles on National Human Rights Institutions. The statute defines human rights as rights relating to life, liberty, equality, and dignity guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in international covenants enforceable by Indian courts. The MyGov campaign platform centralizes public access to NHRC informational resources, including administrative publications, human rights webcasts, complaint registration guidelines, and updates on inquiry proceedings. The objective is to make grievance redressal pathways transparent and inform the public about statutory investigations into human rights issues. Operating expenses and outreach initiatives are financed through statutory Grants-in-Aid provided by the Union Government, ensuring the agency maintains channels to publish independent findings regarding civil and socioeconomic compliance.

campaigns.ministry: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
campaigns.goals: Increase public understanding of applied artificial intelligence across sectors; conduct public consultations regarding ethical AI standards; promote citizen engagement through technical quizzes on indigenous AI models.
campaigns.funding_information: Funded through the national IndiaAI Mission budget approved by the Union Cabinet and administered by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY).
campaigns.summary: The AI Impact campaign comprises public awareness and consultation initiatives organized in conjunction with the India-AI Impact Summit 2026, held at Bharat Mandapam. Coordinated by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology within the framework of the IndiaAI Mission, the campaign focuses on the governance, development, and social deployment of artificial intelligence. Its core public components include open stakeholder consultations on ethical deployment frameworks, an online AI Responsibility Pledge, and contests covering digital storytelling and branding for national AI initiatives. The portal provides links to sector-specific AI deployments implemented across diverse Union ministries, including language translation models for Indian regional languages and public dataset repositories. The primary administrative objective is to evaluate citizen input on technological policy, explain computational infrastructure investments, and foster baseline digital literacy regarding artificial intelligence, supported by central allocations under the IndiaAI budget. It functions to bridge the technical divide between policymakers and software developers within India.

campaigns.ministry: Ministry of Law and Justice, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
campaigns.goals: Mark the 75th year of the adoption of the Constitution of India; educate the public on Fundamental Duties enumerated under Article 51A; administer video pledges verifying civic commitment; conduct national essay and blog competitions.
campaigns.funding_information: Financed by the Central Government through special commemorative budget allocations for the 75th Constitution Year under the Ministry of Law and Justice.
campaigns.summary: The 'Hamara Samvidhan Hamara Swabhiman' (Our Constitution, Our Self-Respect) campaign was a nationwide commemorative initiative that spanned 2024 and culminated on Constitution Day, November 26, 2025, marking the 75th year since the adoption of the Constitution of India in 1949. Spearheaded by the Ministry of Law and Justice alongside the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, the campaign emphasized public awareness of constitutional duties alongside constitutional rights. The digital MyGov hub directed users to multimedia resources detailing the drafting process led by the Constituent Assembly, interactive modules illustrating Fundamental Duties (such as respecting national symbols and promoting gender equality), and an integrated video pledge platform hosted at constitution75.com. The initiative included academic essay competitions and civic quizzes designed to reinforce legal literacy nationwide, financed through dedicated central appropriations for 75th-anniversary constitutional commemorations. The structure of the campaign was directed toward expanding foundational legal knowledge across rural and urban educational districts.
